topic: CompTIA Network+ (N10-009) certification exam preparation - networking fundamentals, network implementations, network operations, network security, and network troubleshooting, including modern topics like cloud and hybrid networking, SDN/SD-WAN, zero trust/SASE, Wi-Fi 6/6E, and basic network automation
exam_format: A maximum of 90 questions, 90 minutes, delivered at Pearson VUE test centers or online via OnVUE. A mix of multiple choice (single and multiple response) and PERFORMANCE-BASED QUESTIONS (PBQs) that simulate real network configuration and troubleshooting tasks (drag-and-drop, matching, simulations). Passing score is 720 on a scale of 100-900 (a scaled score, not a straight percentage). The certification is valid for three years and is renewable through CompTIA's Continuing Education (CE) program. Exam fee is approximately USD 399 for a single voucher at current US retail pricing (CompTIA raised prices across its lineup in mid-2026; a voucher with retake assurance is higher); present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current CompTIA pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE', plus scenario/task-style items that mirror the exam's performance-based questions (subnetting, choosing ports/protocols, reading topologies, applying the troubleshooting methodology)
audience: Early-career network technicians, help-desk and IT support staff, junior network/systems administrators, and anyone building foundational networking skills or preparing for a networking or cybersecurity career. CompTIA recommends about 9-12 months of networking experience or CompTIA A+ level knowledge, though no formal prerequisite is required. A strong foundational companion to the CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701) and SecAI+ courses already in this catalog, and useful groundwork before cloud-networking topics in the AWS and Azure courses.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Networking Fundamentals
domains.notes: The heaviest domain and the conceptual backbone. The OSI model and the TCP/IP stack; ports and protocols (HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, DHCP, FTP/SFTP, SSH, SMTP/IMAP/POP3, SNMP, NTP, RDP, and their port numbers); IPv4 addressing and SUBNETTING (CIDR, subnet masks, private vs public, APIPA), IPv6 addressing; network topologies and types (LAN/WAN/PAN, star/mesh, three-tier and spine-leaf, SDN and SD-WAN); cloud and virtualization concepts (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, public/private/hybrid, VPC, connectivity). Choosing the correct protocol, port, address, or topology for a described requirement.

domains.name: Network Implementations
domains.notes: Deploying network infrastructure: routing and switching (VLANs, trunking, STP, routing concepts, static vs dynamic routing, OSPF/EIGRP/BGP awareness, NAT/PAT); wireless standards and design (802.11 including Wi-Fi 6 and 6E, frequencies and channels, SSIDs, antennas, security modes); physical media and connectors (copper and fiber cabling types, transceivers, ethernet standards); and network appliances (routers, switches, firewalls, load balancers, access points, and their placement). Choosing the correct implementation for a described network build.

domains.name: Network Operations
domains.notes: Keeping networks running: documentation and diagrams, network monitoring (SNMP, syslog, flow data, baselines), high availability and disaster recovery (redundancy, failover, load balancing, backups), and organizational processes (change management, IP address management, SLAs). Basic NETWORK AUTOMATION concepts (scripting, APIs, infrastructure as code) introduced in the 2026 update. Choosing the correct operational practice or monitoring approach for a described scenario.

domains.name: Network Security
domains.notes: Securing the network: core concepts (confidentiality/integrity/availability, ZERO TRUST and SASE, defense in depth), physical and logical security, common attacks (DoS/DDoS, on-path/MITM, spoofing, VLAN hopping, rogue devices, social engineering) and mitigations, and hardening (segmentation, ACLs, port security, 802.1X/NAC, firewalls, VPNs and IPsec, wireless security). Choosing the correct security control or mitigation for a described threat.

domains.name: Network Troubleshooting
domains.notes: Diagnosing and resolving issues using the CompTIA TROUBLESHOOTING METHODOLOGY (identify the problem, establish a theory, test, plan, implement, verify, document). Cable and connectivity issues, common tools (ping, traceroute/tracert, nslookup/dig, ipconfig/ifconfig, netstat, tcpdump, cable testers, protocol analyzers), and troubleshooting wireless, routing/switching, and service (DNS/DHCP) problems. Choosing the correct next troubleshooting step or tool for a described symptom.

extra_guidance: CompTIA Network+ (N10-009) is one of the most popular foundational IT certifications and a common on-ramp to networking and cybersecurity careers. This course targets the CURRENT N10-009 (V9) version - note clearly that N10-009 replaced the older N10-008 and reflects 2026 updates: expanded cloud and hybrid networking, software-defined networking and SD-WAN, zero trust and SASE, modern wireless (Wi-Fi 6 and 6E), and basic network automation. The exam includes PERFORMANCE-BASED QUESTIONS (PBQs) that simulate real tasks, so practice questions MUST include scenario/task-style items - subnetting problems, port/protocol matching, reading a topology, and applying the troubleshooting methodology - not just recall. Teach the fundamentals rigorously: the OSI model, TCP/IP, ports and protocols with their numbers, IPv4/IPv6 addressing and SUBNETTING (this is heavily tested - include worked subnetting examples), cabling and connectors, wireless, routing/switching (VLANs, STP, NAT), network services (DNS, DHCP), security, and troubleshooting. Labs are READ-AND-UNDERSTAND walkthroughs (subnet a network, read a routing table, trace a packet's path, apply the 7-step troubleshooting method, configure a VLAN conceptually, choose the right tool for a symptom) - the exam is about understanding and applying networking concepts, not vendor-specific CLI mastery; make that explicit and keep examples vendor-neutral. The five domain names and weights above are CompTIA's official N10-009 exam objectives - use them verbatim. Note the 3-year validity and CompTIA Continuing Education renewal, and the recommended CompTIA A+ level or 9-12 months of experience. Cover classic Network+ traps: OSI layer identification, common port numbers, subnet-mask/CIDR math, TCP vs UDP, security groups of protocols, straight-through vs crossover, single-mode vs multi-mode fiber, and the ORDER of the troubleshooting methodology steps. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 399, raised in mid-2026, varies by region and voucher type) and advise verifying current CompTIA pricing and the latest exam objectives. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 90-minute, up-to-90-question time-management strategy that budgets time for PBQs. Scan the practice bank for stray vendor-specific or other-exam terms before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
